TELLURIDE FILM FESTIVAL 2026

This year’s festival wrapped on Monday, September 7 — and an amazing, wild set of movies is coming to theaters soon.

The big secret reveal was Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s mind-blowing documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, You Can See Everything.

The Oscar race is on! I’m looking at John Malkovich, Sandra Hüller, Andrew Scott, John Turturro, and others. I spoke to some of them today (7 Sept); they’re all self-deprecating but we know they want (and deserve) the recognition!

THE METHOD

Why five? Why seven?

A rating system should distinguish meaningful differences without pretending subjective judgments are laboratory measurements.

01

Why five categories?

We watch movies for different reasons. These five categories delineate those reasons—and they matter more than the aggregate average. It makes more sense to consider a movie along these dimensions than to reduce it to one oversimplified score.

Any movie that receives a 5 or higher in any category is recommended.

02

Why 0–7?

Seven is the maximum number of meaningful differentiations we can make in a subjective judgment. Beyond that, we are splitting hairs and implying precision that isn't really there.

03

What is 7+?

Seven is the maximum category rating: outstanding, best-in-class. A handful of historical 8s are shown as 7+—a special designation for an accomplishment so extraordinary it sets a new standard.

ORIGINALITY / VOICE

Does it have something to say?

Is this an important movie, made by someone who really has something to say?

DEGREE OF DIFFICULTY

How hard was the swing?

How hard was it to bring this vision to the screen?

ARTISTRY / CINEMATOGRAPHY

Look. Sound. Craft.

How does it look and sound?

EMOTIONAL RESONANCE

Did it make you FEEL?

Does it make you FEEL? If it’s a comedy, did you laugh? If it’s a horror film, were you really scared?

PLOT / STORY / ACTING

Are we going somewhere?

Is this team skillfully taking you somewhere?

THE MIKE SCALE

Compact on purpose.

Component ratings are integers. The aggregate may be decimal because it averages five integer judgments.

1Very poor
2Poor
3Below average
4Solid
5Very good
6Excellent
7Outstanding
7+New standard
